extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers, computational creativity researchers, creative-writing evaluation researchers, seminar attendees
extracted.subtask_description: Framework and evaluation procedure for assessing the creativity of short stories using the Torrance Test of Creative Writing (TTCW), applying human expert judgments and comparing LLM-generated work to professional authors. Focus is on product-oriented creativity measurement and the validity of automated (LLM) assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Torrance Test of Creative Writing (TTCW)
rubrics_metrics.description: TTCW consists of 14 binary tests organized into the original dimensions of Fluency, Flexibility, Originality, and Elaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed as a product-oriented analogue to the Torrance Test of Creative Thinking (TTCT); used to evaluate creativity of stories (48 stories in study) by scoring pass/fail on each of 14 tests. Designed to be applied by human experts (and tested with automated assessors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluency
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the original TTCW dimensions (listed among Fluency, Flexibility, Originality, and Elaboration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the TTCW's organizational structure; the abstract does not provide subtest definitions here but treats Fluency as a distinct dimension to be measured by one or more binary tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the original TTCW dimensions (listed among Fluency, Flexibility, Originality, and Elaboration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the TTCW's organizational structure; intended to capture variety/shift in ideas or approaches in a piece, measured via TTCW binary tests (no further detail in abstract).

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the original TTCW dimensions (listed among Fluency, Flexibility, Originality, and Elaboration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the TTCW's organizational structure; intended to capture novelty or uniqueness in creative writing, measured via TTCW binary tests (no further detail in abstract).

rubrics_metrics.name: Elaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the original TTCW dimensions (listed among Fluency, Flexibility, Originality, and Elaboration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the TTCW's organizational structure; intended to capture detail and development in the work, measured via TTCW binary tests (no further detail in abstract).

rubrics_metrics.name: Binary test pass/fail scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: TTCW's 14 tests are binary (pass/fail) rather than graded on a continuous scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables simple counting of passed tests to compare works (the study reports LLM-generated stories pass 3–10× fewer TTCW tests than professional stories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consensual Assessment Technique (human expert judgments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of the Consensual Assessment Technique to implement a human assessment of stories using TTCW.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study recruited 10 creative writing experts to assess 48 stories using TTCW; implies that expert consensus is the reference standard for TTCW evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated assessment validity (LLM assessors vs experts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploration of the use of LLMs as assessors to automate TTCW evaluation; reported that none of the LLMs positively correlate with the expert assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as a caution/criterion about the current (lack of) validity of automated LLM-based judgments compared to human experts when applying TTCW.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptualization: creativity as product vs process
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between TTCT (measures creativity as a process) and TTCW (proposes measuring creativity as a product).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides choice of evaluation approach: TTCW is intended for product-oriented assessment of finished creative texts, rather than process-focused measures.
